# Section 020: Platform Automation With Operators

The reader learns what makes a custom resource do something: a controller running a reconcile loop. Using the Prometheus Operator, an operator from the CNPE tool list, the reader follows a `Prometheus` custom resource to the StatefulSet, Service and Secrets it creates, reads status conditions and observedGeneration, and sees how finalizers and owner references control deletion. It sits after CRDs because it reads the status and subresources defined there, and before Crossplane because Crossplane is itself a set of operators.

**Curriculum item covered:** Using Kubernetes Operators for Platform Automation and Integration

---

## What You Will Master

- Name the controller, CRDs and RBAC objects an operator installs, from the cluster
- Trace a custom resource to the objects its controller created through ownerReferences
- Read status.conditions and compare observedGeneration with metadata.generation to judge whether the controller has acted
- Find why a reconcile failed from conditions, events and the controller's logs
- Show that the controller restores an owned object that was changed or deleted by hand
- Predict which dependent objects the garbage collector deletes when an owner is deleted
- Choose between foreground, background and orphan cascading deletion with kubectl delete --cascade
- Explain why an object with a finalizer stays in Terminating and which controller must remove the finalizer
- Diagnose an object stuck in Terminating and fix the cause instead of removing the finalizer by hand

---

## The Learning Path

### 1. Read An Operator's Reconcile Loop
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Read An Operator's Reconcile Loop](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-020/module-01/playground` — kind cluster (Kubernetes 1.35) with the Prometheus Operator 0.94.1 installed from its bundle in `default`. In namespace `starfleet`, a ServiceAccount `prometheus` with RBAC and a `Prometheus` resource `starfleet` (one replica, small memory request) that is Available, plus a second `Prometheus` resource `broken` that references a ServiceAccount that does not exist, so its pods are never created and its conditions say why. The `scout` Deployment and Service run in `starfleet` with a ServiceMonitor.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS019.git -c sections/section-020/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Manage Deletion With Finalizers And Owner References
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Manage Deletion With Finalizers And Owner References](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-020/module-02/playground` — kind cluster (Kubernetes 1.35) with the Prometheus Operator 0.94.1 installed and a `Prometheus` resource `starfleet` that owns its StatefulSet, Service and Secrets. Namespace `starfleet` also has a ConfigMap `scout-settings` that carries a custom finalizer `platform.starfleet.io/cleanup` with no controller to remove it, so deleting it leaves it in Terminating on purpose. The TeamEnvironment CRD is installed so the reader can add ownerReferences between custom resources and ConfigMaps by hand.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS019.git -c sections/section-020/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Diagnose And Repair Operator-Managed Resources Capstone — `sections/section-020/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS019.git -c sections/section-020/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** A tenant reports that its Prometheus instance never starts, that a deleted environment left objects behind, and that a namespace cleanup is stuck. The reader reads conditions and operator logs to fix the ServiceAccount reference, adds the missing ownerReference so cleanup cascades, and resolves the stuck Terminating object by restoring the controller that owns its finalizer rather than removing the finalizer by hand.
